chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about a man who intends travel: at what distance does he shorten? He said: in three burud. So this report conforms with the ʿāmmah, and we do not act upon it.

key_terms.السَّفَرَ: travel that affects legal rulings such as shortening salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the narrated report or hadith text
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ بُرُدٍ: three postal stages; a measure of travel distance mentioned in the report
key_terms.مُوَافِقٌ لِلْعَامَّةِ: in agreement with the majority/non-Imami position
key_terms.نَعْمَلُ بِهِ: we act upon it as an authoritative legal basis
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: to shorten the obligatory salat (prayer) during travel

ai.seo_question: At what travel distance does a traveler shorten salat (prayer), and is the report of three burud acted upon?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the legal ruling for the travel distance at which salat (prayer) is shortened. It also indicates that this particular report, though transmitted, is not acted upon because it accords with the view of the ʿāmmah rather than the relied-upon Shia ruling.
